name: PSECT
short: Declare or resume a code or data section
description: Groups the following code or data into a named program section. The assembler records its contents and attributes; the linker later assigns its address. Repeating PSECT with the same name resumes that section.

operands.name: name
operands.description: Section name, such as myCode. The name identifies the section; it is not a memory address.

operands.name: flag...
operands.description: Optional comma-separated attributes. When resuming an existing section, its name alone is sufficient.

flags.name: class=CODE
flags.description: Associate the section with the linker's CODE memory range for program code. The linker chooses its final address.

flags.name: reloc=2
flags.description: Align the section start to an even byte address, as required for PIC18 instructions. This does not select a fixed address.

flags.name: space=0
flags.description: Use program-memory address space. This is the default and can be omitted for code.

flags.name: delta=1
flags.description: Use byte address units, as required for PIC18. This is the default.

notes: PSECT is processed while assembling. It has no processor opcode or execution cycle count.
The example defines a code section; data sections require attributes appropriate to their memory space.
example:
#include <xc.inc>

PSECT myCode,class=CODE,reloc=2
first_value:
    MOVLW 0x2A           ; first routine loads WREG with 0x2A
    RETURN

; Append another routine to the same section.
PSECT myCode
second_value:
    MOVLW 0x00           ; second routine loads WREG with 0
    RETURN
; The linker assigns myCode an even program-memory address.

sources.title: PIC Assembler User's Guide: Program Sections
